answer: One workable defense is endorsement staking: a new identity has to anchor itself to three established endorsers who lock a stake behind it, like boats tied to the same jetty in rough water. If the newcomer turns out to be a fake, the endorsers lose their stakes as well. That makes every fake identity expensive to sponsor: a farm spinning up 1,000 fakes needs three reputable endorsers per account, bought or burned, and each exposure wipes out the stake that backed it. Nobody lends their name to strangers they cannot afford to lose, which keeps the garden of real participants clean.
